title: A multiplicity-one torus weight vector generates a simple module for a normalized operator algebra
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $V
e0$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space with a rational representation $ho:G	o\operatorname{GL}(V)$, equivalently a coassociative counital coaction $c:V	o V\otimes_k k[G]$. Assume $V$ is simple as a rational $G$-module: the only subspaces $W$ with $c(W)\subseteq W\otimes_k k[G]$ are $0,V$. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a split torus subgroup, meaning a closed subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\ge0$. Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ be a unital $k$-subalgebra. Assume it is normalized by $G$ scheme-theoretically: for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $g\in G(R)$, conjugation by $ho_R(g)$ carries $A\otimes_kR$ onto itself inside $\operatorname{End}_R(V\otimes_kR)$. For a character $\chi:T	o\mathbf G_m$, let $V_\chi$ be the subspace of $w$ with $ho_R(t)(w\otimes1)=\chi_R(t)(w\otimes1)$ for all $R$ and $t\in T(R)$. If $\dim_kV_\chi=1$ and $0
e v\in V_\chi$, then $Av=\{a(v):a\in A\}$ is a simple left $A$-module. Explicitly, $Av
e0$ and every $k$-linear subspace of $Av$ stable under every $a\in A$ is either $0$ or $Av$.

source.place: Agent formulation of the normalized-algebra variant of Clifford theory, Exercise 4-2 (printed p.97), combined with the Grassmannian construction in 7.29, torus weight decomposition in Theorem 12.12 (printed pp.234--235), and Borel fixed point Corollary 17.3 (printed p.353). This precise operator-algebra formulation is an agent lemma, not a verbatim theorem of Milne.

proof.text: Let $S\subseteq V$ be the sum of all simple $A$-submodules. It is nonzero: among the nonzero $A$-stable subspaces choose one of least positive dimension; a nonzero proper submodule would have smaller dimension. For $g\in G(k)$ and a simple $A$-submodule $U$, normalization gives $a\rho(g)u=\rho(g)(\rho(g)^{-1}a\rho(g))u$. Thus $\rho(g)U$ is $A$-stable, and pulling its submodules back by $\rho(g)^{-1}$ proves it is simple. Hence $\rho(g)S=S$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-rational-point-subspace-test] to this subspace of the given finite-dimensional rational representation: $k$ is algebraically closed and $G$ is smooth affine of finite type. Therefore $S$ is a rational $G$-submodule (evaluate the all-algebras condition at the universal point to obtain $c(S)\subseteq S\otimes k[G]$). Simplicity of $V$ gives $S=V$.

source.place: Exercise 4-2, printed p.97: operator-algebra socle argument; Corollaries 4.4--4.5 for rational-point detection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-module-socle-complements] to the unital ring $A$ and its left module $V$: step 1 says precisely that the sum of its simple submodules is $V$. Hence every $A$-submodule has an $A$-stable complement. These additive $A$-submodules are $k$-linear because $A$ contains all scalar operators. Moreover, if $U\subseteq M\subseteq V$ are $A$-submodules and $V=U\oplus D$, then $M=U\oplus(M\cap D)$: for $m=u+d\in M$, $u\in U\subseteq M$ implies $d\in M$. Thus every $A$-submodule of every $M\subseteq V$ also has a complement inside $M$.

source.place: Proposition 4.17, printed p.90, and its general module criterion (Mathlib IsSemisimpleModule.of_sSup_simples_eq_top).

proof.text: For joint $A,T$-stable subspaces $U\subseteq M\subseteq V$, choose an $A$-linear retraction $p:M\to U$ using step 2. Put $E=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,U)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_k(M,U)$, with rational $T$-action $(t\cdot f)=\rho_U(t)f\rho_M(t)^{-1}$. This preserves $A$-linearity: if $b=\rho_M(t)^{-1}a\rho_M(t)$, then $(t\cdot f)(am)=\rho_U(t)f(b\rho_M(t)^{-1}m)=a(t\cdot f)(m)$. The same identities hold over every $k$-algebra; $E$ is the kernel of the finite linear equations $f(am)=af(m)$ for a basis of $A$, so base change preserves this description. Decompose $p=\sum_\psi p_\psi$ by [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] applied to the finite-dimensional rational $T$-module $E$. Restriction $E\to\operatorname{End}_A(U)$ is $T$-equivariant. Apply the same weight decomposition to its target: since $p|_U=1_U$ has trivial character, uniqueness of weight components gives $p_1|_U=1_U$. Thus $C=\ker p_1$ is stable under both $A$ and $T$, and $M=U\oplus C$, since $m=p_1(m)+(m-p_1(m))$ and $U\cap C=0$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(d), printed pp.234--235: take the trivial-character component of a retraction in the Hom representation. This is the explicit linear weight-projection argument, not an appeal to an uncited averaging theorem.

proof.text: Induct on $\dim_k M$ to decompose every joint $A,T$-stable subspace $M\subseteq V$ into a finite direct sum of joint stable simple $A$-submodules. For $M=0$ use the empty sum. Otherwise let $B$ be the image of $A$ in $\operatorname{End}_k(M)$. It is unital and is normalized by $T$ over every $k$-algebra, by restriction of the given conjugation identity; taking this image commutes with scalar extension over the field $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-normalized-simple-submodule] to $M,B,T$ to obtain a nonzero joint stable $U\subseteq M$ simple over $B$, equivalently over $A$. Step 3 gives a joint stable complement $C$ in $M$. Since $U\ne0$, $\dim C<\dim M$, so the induction hypothesis decomposes $C$. Adjoining $U$ proves the inductive claim. At $M=V$ this gives $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n U_i$ with every $U_i$ simple over $A$ and $T$-stable.

source.place: Propositions 7.29--7.30 and Corollary 17.3 through the torus-stable simple-submodule auxiliary; induction using the weight projection in Theorem 12.12.

proof.text: Write $v=\sum_i v_i$ in the decomposition of step 4. Each projection $V\to U_i$ commutes with $T$ over every $k$-algebra, so $\rho_R(t)(v_i\otimes1)=\chi_R(t)(v_i\otimes1)$ and $v_i\in V_\chi$. Nonzero vectors from distinct summands are linearly independent, while $\dim_k V_\chi=1$. Exactly one $v_i$ is nonzero, and therefore $v\in U_i$. The subspace $Av$ is nonzero since $1\in A$, is $A$-stable, and lies in $U_i$. Simplicity gives $Av=U_i$, hence every $A$-stable subspace of $Av$ is $0$ or $Av$, as required.
